reviews.comment: Worst teacher to have in ACCT 327. He teachers so poorly makes learning 10x harder. Gives many questions on exams that students don't have enough time to work out.

Best professor i've ever had. Genuinely cared so much for his students. I liked the online lectures because I was able to rewatch videos when studying. I went basically every Friday for office hours and he thoroughly explained all my questions. Best choice for 327 in my opinion.

He is really nice, I just didn't like the classroom setup. The class moves pretty fast, and if you get behind on the videos, the lectures don't help because you won't know what he's talking about. His tests are by far the hardest out of all the profs, and it's not close. If you're good at teaching yourself the material, take a different prof.

Explains things clearly, and the practice quizzes end up being way more helpful than the homework. The videos are super straightforward, so picking a few days each week to watch them really helps. Staying on top of the material makes the class a lot easier to manage.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Larkin is super nice and great at teaching the concepts. Prepared us well for his difficult exams. We watched lecture videos outside of class and could then ask him questions in class. Friday class sessions were purely office hours. He definitely cares and wants to see his students do well. He's the best choice for 327!
Great prof and clearly cares about his students doing well. his exams are known for being the hardest out of all the other professors but he sets you up well and prepares you with lots of resources

Best 327 professor from someone who took it 3 times. The reverse classroom allows for self-paced learning, which is necessary for something as difficult as this course. Go to class to get answers and clarifications, otherwise not needed to go. Class is essentially office hours. I recommend him 1000% for this course!

Professor Larkin was great! The class is super intense, but he sets up clear guidelines and gives great advice on how to succeed. It is mostly video-based, which I like. He curves every test up to a 75 average, and is very clear about his grading breakdown. He is open to arguing for points here and there and answers every question thrown at him.
Had to redo Acct 327 and chose to do it over the summer. He make all the expectations clear day one. It was a reverse classroom setting that worked for me.
I had to retake Acct 327 and did it over

Took this in Summer Session 1, Ryan is hands down the best professor I have had at Mays. He cares so much for his students and knows that 327 is a very hard class. He has a flipped format so you watch notes videos outside of class and ask questions in class. He is willing to answer any question no matter how dumb it may seem, and is v knowledgeable

This class is by far the hardest class I have ever taken. I was Blinn Team, so if you're in the same boat as me, know that you will have to work 50 times harder than anyone else. 

So glad it's over, but if you're looking to learn a lot and have a respectful and comprehensible professor, Larkin is definitely the way to go. Good luck!

Hardest class I have ever taken and I barely passed. However, Larkin was open to meeting outside of class and giving me extra tutoring. He was super supportive and believed in me! Flipped formatting for his lectures.

I had to retake his class and I worked extra hard this semester by going to class everyday, staying after class to get my questions answered and doing homework as soon as I got home. You need to put in a lot of effort to get the results you need so get ready to put all your time in this class to succeed. Larkin is an amazing professor and he cares!
Larkin is one of the best and nicest professor I have ever had. However, I have to admit that the course is hard. Larking is really kind and always willing to help and explain to his students.

Ryan is one of my FAVORITE professors at Mays, he truly cares about his students and answers any questions despite how "dumb" they may be. I battled with ACCT 327 with other professors, however, as long as you watch the lecture videos and attend class to get your questions answered, he will dumb it down to an understandable level. Take him for 327!
Very difficult class. Larkin is a good instructor but the content is tough. Exams are weighted heavily.

I busted my butt for this class oh my gya. RYAN LARKIN MY KING! He is the sweetest man I have ever met. He will drop everything for his students. My best advice is to work on practice problems and work them again until you can do them in your sleep. GOOD LUCK you can do it!!

Ryan Larkin is easily a top 3 professor I have had in Mays Business School. If you are not aware this is the hardest class in Mays. I personally think Larkin is also the hardest section. His reverse learning format is amazing to work at your own pace and listen to questions all class. He is caring and knows how hard this class is and does his best.

Be careful with this professors class. He is a great professor who is helpful, but he could also be the worst for you. All content is in video lectures, so if your a serial procrastinator, I would consider taking a different prof. Otherwise, if your responsible, or need time off for a job, I highly recommend him. Also a very nice grader on tests.

Professor Larkin is 100% the best professor for this class. It is a difficult class however he is extremely clear on what you can expect for exams and wants to help you understand the concepts in any way he can. Larkin does flipped classroom so you can feel free to ask as many questions as you have in class. TAKE LARKIN YOU WONT REGRET IT!

Accounting 327 is considered one of the most difficult classes in the business school due to a required, low average GPA range. It is a weed out class, but Professor Larkin gives you the tools and opportunities to succeed if you want to. It is time intensive and you'll want to attend all lectures, but he is fair and the best teacher for this class.

Professor Larkin is an outstanding professor and person. Always has an open ear to help if you need it and is wicked smart. My small qualm is that his class layout isn't for everyone. It's lectures at home and questions for class. If you're cool with that, then this is the course for you. It's hard material, but he gives you the tools for success.

Truly ask yourself if you would enjoy watching videos to learn accounting. If you do, take Larkin, if you don't, take someone else. His exams are hard, but you will learn a lot. Read the textbook, watch the videos, do the practice problems/exams, and you should get a good grade. He rambles a bit, but is super knowledgeable. Dedicate time to 327.

Made this account just to rate Larkin. He's the best you're gonna get regarding a professor for ACCT 327. The class just sucks in general but he makes it less sucky. Other professors make the class "easier" to take but Larkin makes it actually understandable. He is really wants you to succeed it just depends on what grade you want in this class.

Larkin was a great professor! Made tax easy to understand as you can tell he really cares about it. The quizzes were never that challenging and there is a group project at the end of the year that isn't too bad. If you show up to class and do some extra practice at home, no way you shouldn't do well in this class!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bro take this class in the summer! expeditiously curves the exams LOL but it is a hard class! i got a C because i was taking 2 other summer classes and working like 35hrs a week on top of everything. im also a finance major so i only wanted a C in the class anyway. a B/A is doable tho! just dont do what i did if u want higher. i studied 30hrs/week.

Larkin's class is the the pathway for success for finance or PPA. Material is hard and tricky but you'll learn so much afterwards and you're thank all the previous ratings if you take his class! TAKE HIM if you hate powerpoints.

Larkin sure knows his accounting. This class is a HUGE time commitment, but if you stay ahead in the lecture videos, go to class to ask questions, and start studying early an A is definitely possible. I would recommend doing the HW, practice problems, and practice exams prior to an exam to understand all the material and concepts. You got this!

This class is hard as hell no matter what professor you have. However, Professor Larkin is super passionate for not only his students but also accounting. He truly cares about the success of the students and for them to understand the material. I wish he would teach ACCT 328 this semester :(
Larkin has saved me through Acct 327. He truly cares about his students and wants to help you in any way possible. Love this professor!!! He deserves the world.

If you struggle with a flipped classroom schedule, you WILL NOT be successful in this course. You watch his lecture videos from a couple of years ago that are informational, but not effective when trying to learn so much. He means well, but going to class was a complete waste of time given he doesn't lecture, so get ready to teach yourself!

Difficult class but if you take it during the summer 15-20 hours a week should get you a B and 25-30 hours a week should get you an A. Professor Larkin is a very fair grader and gives you partial credit for everything he can. Your grade will be directly correlated to the time you put into the class. Good luck!
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Larkin is a great teacher, but not as good of a person. Sent a large number of students to the Aggie Honor Council after having misspoke about the rules for a test, and then arbitrated with students to get them to admit guilt and scaring them away from trying their case with the honor council. Very disappointed in him as an Aggie.

AMAZING PROF. Take Larkin, he is so respected and makes this difficult class more manageable. No timed quizzes, you can watch his lectures as many times as you want, easy weekly homework, one project about a 10-k form towards the end. You can manage the A or B as long as you follow the little calendar he makes for his students and come to class.

Class is just hard. Going to a tutor could help, but no doubt it requires a lot more work on your behalf. He curves pretty well until Q drops. However the class average will increase leading to a smaller curve. Requires more than just working problems, you have to understand the material. He is by far the best prof though. He actually cares.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is a flipped learning class where you learn the materials by watching pre-recorded lectures and come to class asking questions. This is not my preferred method of learning so I struggled. But Larkin does his best to answer questions and provide help where needed. Averages for all tests were below 75, but he curved up the average to a 75.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This is probably the toughest class some of you will take, but Prof. Larkin will really do his best to make sure you understand what you're doing. His exams are tough and the bulk of your grade. He's one of the best profs I've had, but his class is just hard. No way around it. I got a B without tutor john, but it required a LOT of work. Study hard
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ryan is arguably one of the best professors I've had so far in college. He genuinely cares about everyone and makes sure that he offers many opportunities for students to succeed. The class itself requires extremely large amounts of time, but a B shouldn't be too hard to get, an A will require much more work (a couple hours of studying every day).
Larkin is passionate about his students and does his best to ensure that his students understand the material at a fundamental level.
This was a very tough course. Ryan does a great job at communicating his expectations, and studying with the tutors at FlowLearn really helped as well!

Often I include gradeing habits in my reviews, but for ACCT327, the department mandates a poor GPA distribution for all the teachers. It is a terribly difficult class, but Larkin is a great and very knowledgeable prof. You can tell he doesn't take pleasure in giving bad grades like some other teachers. Helpful and always available. Take him!
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: ACCT 327 was by far one of the hardest if not hardest courses I have taken. Ryan's lectures were amazing and tried to make sure everyone understand before moving on. If not, he was very accessible outside class, and even more so during the COVID-19 situation. I definitely would not have done as well if I had a different professor!
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the HARDEST class in the business school. You have to study every day and do every practice problem available to pass. Exams are extremely difficult but professor Larkins teaching is amazing!

Larkin is a great professor and really loves accounting. He is an incredibly nice guy and really tries to make sure his students learn the material. You can tell he loves his job and works towards making his class as straight forward as possible. Acct 327 is just a hard class but Larkin is a fair grader and a great guy.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I contemplated about jumping in front of an Aggie Spirit bus, not to have my tuition paid for.. but so I wouldnt have to go to go class.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Larkin is easily one of the best professors I have had. He teaches the course very well, but the course material is extremely hard. Once you understand the material by studying for hours, you get to the test and the questions are harder than any previous problem you have seen. Larkin is a must take for this course, but be ready.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Ryan is one of the best professors in Mays. If you have the chance to take him do it! He takes a long time to get you exam grades back but he checks every single thing to try to give people partial credit. Always genuine and cares about his students.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Take Ryan for 327 if you have the chance! He is accessible, fair, and helpful. Truly one of my favorite professors! He does a great job of simplifying tricky material in a way that makes it easier to digest and retain. Cannot recommend him enough!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Ryan is an amazing guy. He genuinely cares about his students. He take about a week to grade exams but that's because he grades with the intention of giving every point of partial credit he can. He hold quiz reviews and works the problems out for you. He is such a nice guy and actually wants you to succeed.

HIGHLY recommend if you are taking 327. He knows the class is a SOB but does everything within his power to help you. Gives quiz answers if you attend the review sessions. Very generous on giving credit for workout. Its common for him to stay up until 3am to grade tests just to make sure he grades the tests fairly. One of the coolest guys in Mays

Prof. Larkin is a really good instructor. I don't think the department realizes the value he adds. They'd rather pay PHDs more who don't even practice what they teach. Research schools.. SMH. Takes a long time to grade exams, but that is only because he wants to make sure your errors don't compound and you make the highest grade possible.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Larkin is the best prof at Mays in my humble opinion. He dedicates so much for his students to be successful with his office hours and how he plans his lectures. I really liked the class and he was the first professor that I had that actually seemed to care about his students.

Really good professor. Gave many opportunities to get his help outside of class or go over any test. Go to class, take notes, study very hard for the tests. Not an easy class by any means but if you need to take it I would take Larkin.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Ryan is probably my favorite professor at A&M so far. I'm not an accounting wiz and it's not really something that comes natural to me. He taught in a way that made me feel comfortable to ask questions & he genuinely wanted us to learn. 327 is hard - but Ryan grades incredibly generously on your workout. He really helped me get into PPA. He's great
One of the better 327 professors, don't take if you have testing anxiety. Takes over a week to grade any given test

Ryan goes by Ryan, so get used to calling him by his first name. He is very clear on what it takes to be successful in his class, and he seems to genuinely want students to be successful. Ryan makes 327 as simple as possible and explains every concept very thoroughly so it can be understood by everyone. On of my all Time Favorites. VERY FUNNY!

He understands that 327 is a shaft and tries his best to help the class. He holds regular office hours and is very accessible outside of the classroom. The class is hard, rework the practice tests . Do your best to get a 100% on the quizzes, go to office hours (he works them out). I watched the online lectures to refresh my memory on the material.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took him in his first semester of teaching 327. He had not taught it before, but he did warn us at the beginning of the summer that we would be his "guinea pigs" for this class & that he would curve accordingly. The class itself is hard & probably not easier with another prof. He cares a lot though, he even held office hours on a Sunday once.
